question: Should exact requester consumption be terminal delivery proof for descendant runs even when the requester's later outward send fails?
rationale: That choice changes the durable meaning of delivered and determines whether descendant retries are intentionally suppressed; tests cannot establish the intended product boundary.

options.title: Accept consumption with proof
options.body: Treat exact matched requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery, but require live persisted-state and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Credit descendants only after the requester result is successfully delivered outward, preserving descendant retry when the final send fails.

options.title: Use durable inbox semantics
options.body: Pause this mechanism and resolve consumed-versus-undelivered state through the broader durable completion inbox or spool contract.

recommendation.title: Accept consumption with proof
recommendation.body: Treat exact matched requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery, but require live persisted-state and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged descendant-gating work is the strongest available history signal for the affected delivery semantics.
